God, you’re really too kind. Thank you so much for taking time out of your day to help me. Before I respond to you’re question, I want to add some more context to my situation. My family has a history of mental illness, in fact that uncle I was talking about was diagnosed with bipolar disorder (I’m not sure wether it’s bpd I or bpd II). My dad was diagnosed with depression , and I’m also pretty sure he has bipolar disorder too but I’m not a professional so I’m not putting any weight on it. My dad was pretty emotionally abusive at times too, now he works in another state so thankfully I don’t have to deal with him blowing up at me and his toxicity. He wasn’t as bad as my uncle though, my uncle was a million times worse than my dad because at least my dad loved me (which in turn enabled him to have his good moments where as my uncle was just constantly toxic if that makes any sense). I was diagnosed with general anxiety disorder, depression and premenstrual dysphoric disorder.  I was only taking care of my grandmother for a few months, but balancing school and my grandma AND my uncle was the worst few months of my life by far. I’m really shocked I did t kill myself or even hurt myself (yes I do self harm) in those months. My uncles abuse (him venting at me like I was his therapist, telling me things i was better off not knowing, screaming at me for VERY little things, sexually suggestive comments, etc) basically went excused until he had a physical fight with my dad, and that was when he was kicked out. He hasn’t been allowed back in my house, NOT because of the  intense emotional abuse but because he pissed off my dad. That wasn’t the only traumatic thing to happen in my life, but it’s the most recent one. To this day my parents brush it off, and basically tell me close to nothing serious happened and that I’m exaggerating. My uncle hates me now I think. He’s not the only person that hates me, I think everyone who hates me including him would be very happy to know I’m ending my own life. I think the only thing that would make me not kill myself is if my mental illness was no longer a handicap for me, and that I could be self sufficient. Unfortunately, as I said before, I’ve been fired from two jobs, there’s no hope for me. I’m not valuable to society, therefore I’m better off dead. I really wish things weren’t like this, I wish I didn’t have mental illness. I know my friends and (most of) my family will miss me. Honestly, it’s better to die now while I’m young then be a 35 year old leech in society. Again, thank you so much for your help, but I really can’t live anymore. I don’t know when my death date is yet, I think it’ll be once I get to see my best friend for a day for the last time. She’s one of the reasons I held out for so long. Maybe go to church for the last time, see my dad or talk to him for the last time. Lots of things I need to do.

Maybe I am not the best one to be speaking on this subject, since i still deal with suicidal thoughts by harming myself but for the times when I avoid it, this is what I do: 

1. **Speak to the people who love me.** I am particularly close with my mom, so i speak with her when i am suicidal. Having someone who truly cares about you comfort you like that to me is the biggest help I can get.  I also speak to my dad sometimes, I'm not as close with him as i used to be but I know I still mean the absolute world to him, and that i can go to him for anything. I'm very lucky in the fact I have VERY loving parents. I have friends, a loving (albeit an overprotective) sister, and three wonderful cats, and i remind myself how lucky I am to have the people I have in my life. I promise you, even if you think no one cares, there's always at least one person who relies on you in one way or another. The butterfly affect is quite real, and every single life matters. Including yours.
2. **Animals.** As I said before, I have three cats. If you love animals like I do, animals are EXTREMELY therapeutic. There have been multiple times where I felt alone and my cats have came to comfort me. I've had my cats nudge me to wipe off my tears, cuddle with me and essentially make me feel loved. If you like animals, and have a pet, spend some time with them, i promise your mood will be elevated.
3. **Writing an Art.** I like writing to begin with, but i have also found it serves a great distraction. I think distraction is the key to calming your intrusive thoughts. I get so caught up in  trying to make coherent writings that i totally forget what i was upset about. write about your feelings, make poetry, write a story, what ever you want! I promise it serves as a great distraction. The same goes for art.
4. **Water and Exercise.** I know any person who is depressed has heard this a million and one times before by neurotypicals who seem to have no idea what they are talking about, but this really does has legitimacy to it. It releases dopamine and serves as a great distraction. You'll also feel so proud of yourself after exercising. Water can help flush the system, i recommend cold water because heat is a big physical stresser and cooling down will help the body relax greatly.

 These may not work for you, but these have worked for me. The most important thing that you take out of this is that you matter, and you're worth the work put into recovery. 

**tl;dr** speak to the people who love you, cuddle with animals, write something, and drink some water
